content: The interaction between erythromycin base and other drugs is complex and requires careful consideration. Below is a detailed explanation of the interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Paclitaxel Protein-Bound: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of paclitaxel protein-bound by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Pacritinib: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pacritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 3. Palbociclib: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of palbociclib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Paliperidone: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of paliperidone through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 5. Palovarotene: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or reduce the palovarotene dose by 50% if unavoidable. 6. Panobinostat: Both erythromycin base and panobinostat prolong the QTc interval. Panobinostat prescribing information advises against co-administration with QTc-prolonging drugs. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Pantothenic Acid: Erythromycin base decreases the level or effect of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 8. Parecoxib: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of parecoxib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Paromomycin: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of paromomycin through P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 10. Paroxetine: Both erythromycin base and paroxetine prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 11. Pasireotide: Both erythromycin base and pasireotide prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Pazopanib: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pazopanib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Pemetrexed: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pemetrexed by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Penicillin G and VK: Erythromycin base decreases the effects of penicillin G and VK due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Pentamidine: Both erythromycin base and pentamidine prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Pentobarbital: Pentobarbital decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The interaction is minor, but caution is advised. 17. Perphenazine: Both erythromycin base and perphenazine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Pexidartinib: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pexidartinib via CYP3A4 inhibition. Pexidartinib can cause hepatotoxicity. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Phenindione: Erythromycin base increases the effects of phenindione by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Phenobarbital: Phenobarbital decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The interaction is minor, but caution is advised. 21. Phenytoin: Phenytoin decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. Pimozide: Both erythromycin base and pimozide prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin base also increases pimozide levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 23. Pioglitazone: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pioglitazone via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Piperacillin: Erythromycin base decreases the effects of piperacillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Pitavastatin: Erythromycin base increases the toxicity of pitavastatin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Do not exceed 1 mg/day of pitavastatin. 26. Pomalidomide: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pomalidomide via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Ponatinib: Ponatinib increases erythromycin base levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Posaconazole: Both erythromycin base and posaconazole prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin base also increases posaconazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Pravastatin: Erythromycin base increases the toxicity of pravastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, increasing the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 30. Prednisolone and Prednisone: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of prednisolone and prednisone via P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Pretomanid: Pretomanid increases erythromycin base levels and toxicity. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 32. Primaquine: Both erythromycin base and primaquine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Primidone: Primidone decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base via CYP3A4 induction. The interaction is minor, but caution is advised. 34. Procainamide: Both erythromycin base and procainamide prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 35. Prochlorperazine: Both erythromycin base and prochlorperazine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Promazine: Both erythromycin base and promazine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 37. Promethazine: Both erythromycin base and promethazine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Propafenone: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of propafenone via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Protriptyline: Both erythromycin base and protriptyline prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Pyridoxine: Erythromycin base decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 41. Quetiapine: Both erythromycin base and quetiapine prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin base also increases quetiapine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Quinidine: Both erythromycin base and quinidine prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin base also increases quinidine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 43. Quinine: Both erythromycin base and quinine prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin base also increases quinine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Quinupristin/Dalfopristin: Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 45. Quizartinib: Both erythromycin base and quizartinib prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 46. Rivaroxaban: Erythromycin base increases rivaroxaban levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely, especially in patients with renal impairment. 47. Roflumilast: Erythromycin base increases roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 48. Romidepsin: Both erythromycin base and romidepsin prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin base also increases romidepsin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 49. Rosuvastatin: Erythromycin base increases rosuvastatin toxicity by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Use caution and monitor. 50. Rucaparib: Rucaparib increases erythromycin base levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 51. Rufinamide: Rufinamide decreases erythromycin base levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 52. Ruxolitinib: Erythromycin base increases ruxolitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Sacubitril/Valsartan: Erythromycin base increases valsartan levels by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Sildenafil: Erythromycin base increases sildenafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider starting with a lower dose of sildenafil (25 mg). 55. Simvastatin: Erythromycin base increases simvastatin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of rhabdomyolysis. Co-administration is contraindicated. 56. Siponimod: Both erythromycin base and siponimod prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin base also increases siponimod levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 57. Sirolimus: Erythromycin base increases sirolimus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 58. Sotalol: Both erythromycin base and sotalol prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 59. Stiripentol: Stiripentol increases erythromycin base levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 60. St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases erythromycin base levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 61. Sufentanil: Erythromycin base increases sufentanil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Sulbactam/Durlobactam: Erythromycin base increases sulbactam levels via OATP1 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 63. Sonidegib: Erythromycin base increases sonidegib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 64. Sodium Bicarbonate: Sodium bicarbonate increases erythromycin base levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 65. Sodium Citrate/Citric Acid: Sodium citrate increases erythromycin base levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 66. Sodium Picosulfate: Erythromycin base decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora. Use caution and monitor. 67. Solifenacin: Both erythromycin base and solifenacin prolong the QTc interval. Erythromycin base also increases solifenacin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 68. Sorafenib: Both erythromycin base and sorafenib prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This list highlights the importance of understanding drug interactions when prescribing erythromycin base. Always consult detailed prescribing information and monitor patients closely when combining erythromycin with other medications.
